## How does API work in Pipedrive?

Note: To keep your data secure, it‘s extremely important that your API token is not shared with others. If you believe someone has access to your API token, click “Generate new token“ to create a new one. You’ll need to update any existing API connections with the new token afterward.

To create an API connection between your Pipedrive account and another application, find your personal API key by going to Settings > Personal preferences > API.

Image

Once you have your token, you’ll need a platform to facilitate your API requests, like Postman.

Setting up Postman

Note: Postman isn’t a Pipedrive tool, but it can be used to execute API actions with your Pipedrive account. For an in-depth guide to Postman and how it works, check out their web page.

To use Postman as your API platform, follow this link to our Developer’s corner, then either download Postman using the provided link or click “Run in Postman“ if you’ve already downloaded it.

Image

After you “fork collection,“ you’ll be taken to the Postman workspace, where you can see the available API requests through Pipedrive on the left.

Image

Creating an API request usually requires a few things:

  * Your API token
  * An endpoint (i.e deals)
  * An HTTP verb (i.e GET)

Note: Pipedrive uses RESTful API Reference, and you can access it along with a list of endpoints and their descriptions on this developer’s page. To see the list of endpoints, click the arrow next to API Reference at the top of the page.

# Authentication

> 📘
> 
> All requests to our API need authentication.

If you're creating an app

Continue to OAuth 2.0 overview.
You can find our step-by-step guide to getting OAuth 2.0 implemented in your app in OAuth authorization .

If you're working with an API token integration

The API token must be provided in the `x-api-token` header for all requests, for example:

[Button: cURL]
    
    `curl --request GET \
    --url "https://companydomain.pipedrive.com/api/v2/deals" \
    --header "x-api-token: 659c9fddb16335e48cc67114694b52074e812e03"`

How to find the API token?

> 📘
> 
> Keep in mind that an API token is tied to a specific user and company, giving access to all user's data. You can only have one active API token at any time. If you change the API token, all existing integrations using this API token will not be able to make successful requests against our API and stop working.

## What is the API key for?

Jenny Takahara

Last updated: September 3, 2026

The API key is for developers to build integrations between Pipedrive and other services. It requires a level of technical knowledge to use, so should only be used by developers or engineers in your team.
Please also note that, through the API (by using the API key), all data is accessible from your Pipedrive account. That means you shouldn't share the key with anyone you wouldn't also be comfortable sharing data with.
Without the key, your account is perfectly safe, so as long as you don't share the key there is no need to worry.

You can look at this article to learn about where to find your personal API key.

## API Reference

This reference helps you implement the RESTful Pipedrive API. This API uses a JSON format for output and is capable of handling CORS (Cross-Origin Resource Sharing) requests. The API is stateless – all requests are validated against an API token. The API token can be obtained manually from the Pipedrive app.

#### OpenAPI 3

You can click on the "Run in Postman" button below to interact with our API. We have a tutorial for using Pipedrive API in Postman or Insomnia, but if you prefer to use a different tool, you can always import our OpenAPI 3 specification files (available for both v1 and v2 APIs) into your tool of choice. See this article to learn more about Pipedrive API v2. Keep in mind that we'll occasionally update our OpenAPI 3 specification files, so you might need to re-import them from time to time.

## Can all users access the Pipedrive API?

BF

Breandan Flood

Last updated: September 3, 2026

By default, all users in any company account can access the Pipedrive API information for their account.
If you would like to turn off this ability for the global regular users in your Pipedrive account, an admin user can go to Settings > Manage Users > Permission sets.

Select the “Global regular user” permission set and scroll down to the “Tools and setup” section. Then, de-select the “Access their own API token” option to revoke access to the API.

Note: Disabling access to the API will impact users’ ability to export data from their Pipedrive company account and install integrations and apps from the Pipedrive Marketplace, unless the integration doesn’t need the API token and uses OAuth instead.
